import pandas as pd

# List all source file paths
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_65/training_0.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_65/training_1.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_65/training_2.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_65/training_3.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_65/training_4.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_65/training_5.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_65/training_6.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_65/training_7.csv"
]

# Target schema columns in order
target_columns = [
    'movie_display_name',
    'movie_production_year',
    'movie_genre_display_name',
    'movie_financial_summary_production_budget',
    'movie_financial_summary_international_box_office',
    'movie_annual_summary_tickets_sold',
    'movie_video_summary_domestic_dvd_units',
    'movie_acting_role_display_name',
    'movie_theatrical_release_release_date',
    'movie_creative_type_display_name',
    'movie_production_method_display_name',
    'movie_source_display_name',
    'movie_running_time',
    'movie_technical_role_display_name',
    'movie_production_company_display_name',
    'movie_sequel'
]

# Data types for target columns (to ensure consistency)
# From the prompt:
# string: movie_display_name, movie_genre_display_name, movie_acting_role_display_name,
#         movie_theatrical_release_release_date, movie_creative_type_display_name,
#         movie_production_method_display_name, movie_source_display_name,
#         movie_technical_role_display_name, movie_production_company_display_name
# integer: movie_production_year, movie_financial_summary_production_budget,
#          movie_financial_summary_international_box_office, movie_sequel
# float: movie_annual_summary_tickets_sold, movie_video_summary_domestic_dvd_units,
#        movie_running_time

# We'll enforce these types after loading and concatenation.

# Step 1: Load all source CSVs into a list of DataFrames
dfs = []
for file_path in source_files:
    df = pd.read_csv(file_path, index_col=0)
    # All source schemas are identical and match target columns exactly
    # So no renaming or column selection needed here
    dfs.append(df)

# Step 2: Concatenate all source DataFrames (UNION)
combined_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

# Step 3: Enforce target schema columns order and types

# Ensure all target columns exist in combined_df (they do, per prompt)
combined_df = combined_df[target_columns]

# Convert columns to appropriate types with care for missing values

# Integer columns (allow NaN, so use pandas nullable Int64 dtype)
int_cols = [
    'movie_production_year',
    'movie_financial_summary_production_budget',
    'movie_financial_summary_international_box_office',
    'movie_sequel'
]

for col in int_cols:
    # Convert to numeric, coerce errors to NaN, then to nullable Int64
    combined_df[col] = pd.to_numeric(combined_df[col], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')

# Float columns
float_cols = [
    'movie_annual_summary_tickets_sold',
    'movie_video_summary_domestic_dvd_units',
    'movie_running_time'
]

for col in float_cols:
    combined_df[col] = pd.to_numeric(combined_df[col], errors='coerce').astype(float)

# String columns - convert to string, keep NaN as is
str_cols = [
    'movie_display_name',
    'movie_genre_display_name',
    'movie_acting_role_display_name',
    'movie_theatrical_release_release_date',
    'movie_creative_type_display_name',
    'movie_production_method_display_name',
    'movie_source_display_name',
    'movie_technical_role_display_name',
    'movie_production_company_display_name'
]

for col in str_cols:
    combined_df[col] = combined_df[col].astype('string')

# Step 4: Export the combined DataFrame to the target CSV path
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_65/target_multisource_cot.csv"
combined_df.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
